questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

"A. Neither of the two B. proposals were approved C. because the committee found D. both of them to be unsatisfactory."

options.text: both of them to be unsatisfactory.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the use of the plural verb "**were**" with the singular subject "**Neither**."
 
• When "Neither" is used as the subject of a sentence, it is grammatically singular and requires a **singular verb**.
 
• The correct phrase should be "**proposals was approved**," ensuring proper subject-verb agreement.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part B** (Option 2) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Neither of the two **proposals was approved** because the committee found both of them to be unsatisfactory."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "Neither of the two" **– This part correctly sets up the choice between two specific items and serves as the singular subject.
 
• **C: "because the committee found"** – This part is grammatically correct; "committee" is a collective noun acting as a single unit here.
 
• **D: "both of them to be unsatisfactory."** – This part correctly uses "both" to refer back to the two proposals and is grammatically sound.
 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** Although "proposals" is plural, it is the object of the preposition "of," not the subject of the sentence.

questions.question:
**Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.**

"A. He is B. not only intelligent C. and hardworking, D. but also very kind."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses the correlative conjunction "**not only... but also**," which is used to connect two balanced clauses or phrases.
 
• The inclusion of "**and**" in part C is redundant and grammatically incorrect because the "not only" in part B is already waiting to be paired with "but also" in part D.
 
• To maintain the correct correlative structure, the conjunction "and" should be removed or replaced to ensure the two parts of the pair correlate directly.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part C** (Option 3) of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He is **not only intelligent hardworking, but also** very kind." *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Correlative Conjunctions:** These are pairs like *either... or*, *neither... nor*, and *not only... but also*. They must connect grammatically similar elements (parallelism).
 
• **A: "He is"** – This is the subject and helping verb, which is correct.
 
• **B: "not only intelligent"** – This starts the correlative pair correctly.
 
• **D: "but also very kind"** – This completes the correlative pair correctly.
 
• **Parallelism:** When using "not only... but also," ensure that the words following each part of the conjunction are the same part of speech (in this case, adjectives: intelligent/hardworking and kind).

questions.question:
**Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:**

"He has a lot of potential, ______ his lack of discipline may hinder his growth."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**whereas**'.

__
 
• The conjunction "**whereas**" is used to show contrast between two clauses.
 
• In the given sentence, the two parts are contrasting: "He has a lot of potential" contrasts with "his lack of discipline may hinder his growth."
 
• **Options 2, 3, 4**, and 5 are grammatically incorrect or do not fit the context of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"He has a lot of potential, **whereas**__ his lack of discipline may hinder his growth."*

• **Option 2: "unless"** is incorrect because it is used to introduce a condition, not a contrast.
 
• **Option 3: "because"** is incorrect as it introduces a reason, not a contrasting idea.
 
• **Option 4: "albeit"** is incorrect because it means "although" or "even though," and does not fit with the structure of the sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: **All hands on the deck**

options.text: Someone in charge of the deck

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Everyone working together**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"All hands on the deck"** means that everyone is required to work together or contribute to a task, especially in a situation of urgency or importance. (सभी को एक साथ मिलकर काम करना पड़ता है)

 
 
• **Example: **When the company was facing a critical deadline, it was all hands on the deck to complete the project on time.
 

 
• **Correct Explanation:** The idiom emphasizes teamwork and cooperation, especially in situations that demand collective effort. (टीमवर्क और सहयोग पर जोर देना, खासकर जब एक सामूहिक प्रयास की आवश्यकता हो)

 
 
• **Example: **The storm was approaching fast, so it was all hands on the deck to secure the ship.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Everyone working together**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: Someone in charge of the deck **(डेक का प्रभारी व्यक्ति): This is incorrect as the idiom does not refer to a single person but rather to collective teamwork.
 
 
• **Example:** The captain of the ship is responsible for the deck, but this does not align with the idiom's meaning.
 
 

 
• **Option 3: A distraction on the deck **(डेक पर ध्यान भटकाने वाला कुछ): This is incorrect as the idiom does not refer to a distraction but to a coordinated effort.
 
 
• **Example: **There was no distraction on the deck; instead, everyone was focused on the task.
 
 

 
• **Option 4: A difficult task **(एक कठिन कार्य): This is incorrect because the idiom doesn’t refer to the difficulty of the task but rather to the need for collective effort.
 
 
• **Example:** While it was a difficult task, all hands on the deck ensured it was completed successfully.

questions.question:
**Change the following sentence into the Active form:**

"It was believed that the secret formula had been stolen by a rival company."

options.text: A rival company believed that the secret formula had been stolen.
People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula.
The secret formula was stolen by a rival company.
A rival company stole the secret formula, it was believed.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Active voice structure:** The subject performs the action, whereas in the passive voice, the subject receives the action.
 
• The original sentence contains two passive constructions: "It was believed" (Passive reporting) and "had been stolen by a rival company" (Passive main clause).
 
• To convert **"It was believed"** to active, we need a general subject like **"People"** or **"They"** because the original agent is unspecified.
 
• To convert **"had been stolen by a rival company"** to active, the agent **"a rival company"** must become the subject of the verb "had stolen."
 
• Combining these changes results in: "People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"People believed that a rival company had stolen the secret formula."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "A rival company believed that the secret formula had been stolen." – This changes the meaning; it suggests the rival company was the one believing the theft occurred.
 
• **Option 3:** "The secret formula was stolen by a rival company." – This is still in the passive voice and omits the "It was believed" context entirely.
 
• **Option 4:** "A rival company stole the secret formula, it was believed." – While the first part is active, "it was believed" remains a passive construction at the end.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

"I bought **a new pair of jeans and they are already torn."**

options.text: I bought a new pair of jeans and it is already torn
I bought a new pair of jeans and it has already torn
I bought a new pair of jeans and it was already torn
I bought a new pair of jeans and which are already torn

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The subject "**a pair of jeans**" is singular, and therefore, the verb "**is**" must agree with the singular subject.
 
• The correct choice is **Option 1**, where the singular verb "**is**" matches the subject.
 
• **Option 2** ("it has already torn") is grammatically incorrect because "has torn" implies an action performed by the subject, which is not possible for jeans.
 
• **Option 3** ("it was already torn") suggests the jeans were already torn at the time of purchase, which contradicts the intended meaning.
 
• **Option 4** ("and which are already torn") is grammatically awkward and redundant.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"I bought a new pair of jeans and it is already torn."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "it has already torn"** is incorrect because it implies an action performed by the jeans, which is not logical.
 
• **Option 3: "it was already torn"** is incorrect as it contradicts the idea of buying new jeans.
 
• **Option 4: "and which are already torn"** is incorrect due to redundancy and awkward phrasing.

questions.question:
**Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:**

"The government will be implementing the new environmental regulations next month."

options.text: The new environmental regulations will be implemented by the government next month.
The new environmental regulations will be being implemented by the government next month.
The new environmental regulations are being implemented by the government next month.
The new environmental regulations will have been implemented by the government next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Identify the Tense:** The active sentence "will be implementing" is in the **Future Continuous Tense**.
 
• **Passive Structure for Future Continuous:** The formula is **Object + will be + being + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject**.
 
• **Step 1:** Move the object "The new environmental regulations" to the beginning.
 
• **Step 2:** Change the verb "will be implementing" to "will be being implemented."
 
• **Step 3:** Add the agent "by the government" and the time phrase "next month."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The new environmental regulations will be being implemented by the government next month."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "will be implemented" – This is the Future Simple Passive. It misses the continuous "being" aspect.
 
• **Option 3:** "are being implemented" – This is the Present Continuous Passive, which changes the timeframe from future to present.
 
• **Option 4:** "will have been implemented" – This is the Future Perfect Passive, used for actions that will be completed by a certain point.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.**

"My friend told me that she had been thinking about quitting her job but that she had not made a final decision yet."

options.text: My friend said to me, "I was thinking about quitting my job, but I have not made a final decision yet."
My friend said to me, "I have been thinking about quitting my job, but I have not made a final decision yet."
My friend said to me, "I had been thinking about quitting my job, but I had not made a final decision yet."
My friend said to me, "I have been thinking about quitting my job, but I did not make a final decision yet."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** "My friend told me that she had been thinking about quitting her job but that she had not made a final decision yet."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Tense Change (Forward-shifting):**
 
 
• When converting from indirect to direct speech, we move the tenses forward.
 
• The past perfect continuous **"had been thinking"** shifts forward to the present perfect continuous **"have been thinking."**
 
• The past perfect **"had not made"** shifts forward to the present perfect **"have not made."**
 
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The third-person pronoun **"she"** and possessive **"her"** in indirect speech must change to the first-person **"I"** and **"my"** to reflect the original speaker's perspective.
 
 
 
• **Reporting Verb:**
 
 
• The reporting verb **"told me"** is typically converted back to **"said to me"** followed by a comma and quotation marks.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"My friend said to me, 'I have been thinking about quitting my job, but I have not made a final decision yet.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrectly uses the past continuous ("I was thinking") for the first part of the sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** Keeps the verbs in the past perfect ("had been thinking," "had not made"), which would only be used in direct speech if the action had already been completed before another past event.
 
• **Option 4:** Uses the simple past ("did not make") for the second clause, which does not align with the duration/relevance implied by "yet" in this context.

questions.question: In the sentence, “The persistence of such barriers underscores the necessity for institutional reforms aimed at amplifying female representation in executive roles,” the phrase “aimed at amplifying female representation” is:

options.text: an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 2) a participial phrase modifying “reforms”***

 
 
• This is the **correct** answer. The phrase begins with the past participle "aimed." It functions as an adjectival phrase directly describing the noun preceding it, "reforms." It tells us specifically what kind of institutional reforms are necessary—those that are aimed at amplifying female representation.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (a misplaced modifier)**: Incorrect because it is placed perfectly adjacent to the noun it describes ("reforms"), meaning there is no grammatical ambiguity about what is being modified.
 
• **Option 3 (an absolute phrase modifying the entire sentence)**: Incorrect because an absolute phrase typically features a noun or pronoun alongside a participle modifying the whole clause (e.g., "The reforms having passed, the board celebrated"), which doesn't fit the syntax here.
 
• **Option 4 (an infinitive phrase modifying “necessity”)**: Incorrect because an infinitive phrase requires the word "to" followed by the base form of a verb (e.g., "to aim").

__
 
• ***Tense Analysis: Present Tense***

 
 
• The auxiliary (helping) verb used in the sentence is **"is"**, which indicates that the action is occurring in the present tense. If it were past tense, the helping verb would be "was."
 
 
 
• ***Voice Analysis: Passive Voice***
 
 
• In the passive voice, the subject of the sentence is the recipient of the action rather than the doer. Here, the subject **"Their leadership"** receives the action of being characterized.
 
• A passive voice construction requires a form of the "to be" verb paired with a past participle. The phrase **"is characterized"** follows this exact formula.
 
• Additionally, the use of the preposition **"by"** to introduce the actual agents of the action ("a collaborative approach, emotional intelligence, and resilience") is a classic indicator of a passive sentence.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **passive voice, present tense.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (active voice, present tense)**: Incorrect because the subject is receiving the action, not performing it. An active equivalent would be: "A collaborative approach characterizes their leadership."
 
• **Option 3 (active voice, past tense)**: Incorrect due to both voice (it is passive) and tense (it uses "is" instead of "was").
 
• **Option 4 (passive voice, past tense)**: Incorrect because the auxiliary verb "is" places the sentence in the present tense. The past passive equivalent would be "was characterized."

questions.question: The word **“ascendancy”** in the passage most nearly means:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option (2)** i.e. Dominance or rise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"ascendancy"** means occupation of a position of dominant power or influence; a state of rising to power or becoming more dominating. (प्रभुत्व या प्रभाव)

 
 
• **Example: **The party's ascendancy in the political arena was remarkable.
 
 
 
• The closest synonym for **'ascendancy'** is **'dominance or rise'**, which means having a commanding influence or coming into an increased level of power. (प्रभुत्व या उदय)
 
 
• **Example: **The company's rise to market dominance was swift and impressive.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Dominance or rise**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Decline** (पतन): A decrease in quality, quantity, or importance.

 
 
• **Example: **There has been a decline in sales over the past few months.
 
 
 
• **Stagnation** (स्थिरता): The state of not flowing or not moving.
 
 
• **Example: **The local economy showed signs of stagnation despite efforts for development.
 
 
 
• **Separation** (विच्छेद या अलगाव): The action or state of moving or being moved apart.
 
 
• **Example: **The separation of the two companies was completed in January.

questions.question: The phrase **“nuanced reconfiguration”** implies:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the words:***

 
 
• **Nuanced:** This refers to something that has subtle distinctions, delicate variations, or complex layers of meaning. It is the opposite of something basic or simplistic.
 
• **Reconfiguration:** This means the act of rearranging, altering, or restructuring the layout or composition of something.
 
• When combined, a **"nuanced reconfiguration"** indicates a careful, detailed, and intricate process of changing how something is structured. Therefore, "a complex and subtle restructuring" is the precise meaning.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **a complex and subtle restructuring.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (a simplistic rearrangement)**: Incorrect because "nuanced" implies complexity and subtle detail, which directly contradicts the idea of something being "simplistic."
 
• **Option 3 (a chaotic disruption)**: Incorrect because a nuanced approach implies careful, deliberate attention to minor details rather than chaos or random disruption.
 
• **Option 4 (an immediate reversal)**: Incorrect because "reconfiguration" means rearranging parts into a new form, not necessarily going backward or reversing, and "nuanced" does not relate to the speed (immediacy) of the action.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is a major barrier faced by women CEOs and CTOs?

options.text: Unequal access to mentorship and networking opportunities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Analyzing the barriers for women in leadership:***

 
 
• Although the specific passage is not provided, in standard reading comprehension texts addressing women in executive roles (like CEOs and CTOs), a commonly cited systemic barrier is **unequal access to mentorship and networking opportunities**.
 
• Women frequently face challenges in corporate environments due to exclusion from informal networks, "boys' clubs," and a lack of high-level sponsors or mentors, all of which are crucial for career advancement into C-suite positions.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Unequal access to mentorship and networking opportunities.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (Excessive technological knowledge)**: Incorrect because having profound technological knowledge is an asset, particularly for a CTO, rather than a barrier to success.
 
• **Option 2 (Lack of emotional intelligence)**: Incorrect because this is a subjective trait rather than a systemic barrier, and emotional intelligence is increasingly recognized as a key strength in modern leadership.
 
• **Option 4 (Overrepresentation in executive roles)**: Incorrect because women are historically underrepresented, not overrepresented, in top executive positions across most major industries.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentence parts to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. The perfect gift appeared on her screen, so she clicked to add it to her cart.

Q. She typed in her address and credit card details, then checked out.

R. With a final click, her order was placed and confirmed.

S. Now she waits for the package to arrive at her doorstep.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows a chronological sequence of an online shopping experience, moving from item selection to final delivery anticipation.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it initiates the narrative by identifying the object and the first action:
 
 
• "The perfect gift appeared on her screen, so she clicked to add it to her cart."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as the next logical step in the e-commerce process, which is providing the necessary information for the purchase:
 
 
• "She typed in her address and credit card details, then checked out."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** because it describes the finality of the digital transaction:
 
 
• "With a final click, her order was placed and confirmed."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth** as it represents the aftermath of the action—the period of waiting after the order has been successfully processed:
 
 
• "Now she waits for the package to arrive at her doorstep."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"The perfect gift appeared on her screen, so she clicked to add it to her cart. She typed in her address and credit card details, then checked out. With a final click, her order was placed and confirmed. Now she waits for the package to arrive at her doorstep."

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He developed his finger strength and dexterity by practicing his scales and chords daily.

Q. He studied sheet music for hours, learning to play tunes that got harder and harder.

R. He had mastered his new instrument and was now a musician.

S. He played a challenging piece perfectly from memory while performing for his buddies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph describes the progression of a person learning a musical instrument, moving from basic physical training to a final state of mastery.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it establishes the foundation of the learning process—developing the physical dexterity required to play:
 
 
• "He developed his finger strength and dexterity by practicing his scales and chords daily."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as the logical progression from basic exercises to more complex study and increasingly difficult music:
 
 
• "He studied sheet music for hours, learning to play tunes that got harder and harder."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the third sentence** because it represents the climax of his training—the moment he successfully demonstrates his skills in a high-pressure situation:
 
 
• "He played a challenging piece perfectly from memory while performing for his buddies."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the fourth sentence** as it provides the concluding statement, defining his new identity based on the journey described in the previous sentences:
 
 
• "He had mastered his new instrument and was now a musician."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQSR**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He developed his finger strength and dexterity by practicing his scales and chords daily. He studied sheet music for hours, learning to play tunes that got harder and harder. He played a challenging piece perfectly from memory while performing for his buddies. He had mastered his new instrument and was now a musician."

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

"The undercover officer managed to ______ a confession about the gang’s ______ activities."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. "elicit, illicit".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"elicit"** means to draw out a response, answer, or fact from someone, often with effort. (प्राप्त करना, खींचना)
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher tried to elicit answers from the students during the discussion.
 
 
 
• **"Illicit"** refers to something that is illegal, forbidden, or against the rules. (गैरकानूनी, अनुचित)
 
 
• **Example:** The police uncovered an illicit drug operation in the warehouse.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, "elicit" fits the first blank as the officer is trying to draw a confession, and "illicit" fits the second blank as it describes the illegal activities of the gang.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: illicit, elicit**
 
 
• Explanation: The order of these words is incorrect for the context of the sentence.
 
• Meaning: "Illicit" (गैरकानूनी) and "Elicit" (प्राप्त करना).
 
• **Example:** Incorrect usage in this case: "The officer managed to illicit a confession about the gang's elicit activities."
 
 
 
• **Option 3: solstice, solicit**
 
 
• Explanation: These words are unrelated to the context of the sentence.
 
• Meaning: 
 
 
• "Solstice" (अयन): An astronomical event marking the longest or shortest day of the year.
 
• "Solicit" (अनुरोध करना): To ask for or try to obtain something from someone.
 
 
 
• **Example:** 
 
 
• "The summer solstice occurs in June."
 
• "The charity is soliciting donations for the cause."
 
 
 
 
 
• **Option 4: solicit, solstice**
 
 
• Explanation: Same as Option 3, the words are misplaced in the sentence's context.
 
• Meaning: "Solicit" (अनुरोध करना) and "Solstice" (अयन).
 
• **Example:** Incorrect usage in this case: "The officer managed to solicit a confession about the gang's solstice activities."
